spec_features.spec_quote: A study whose output is "here is the model family we can drive into the most distress" ... generates exactly the thing welfare work should be trying to reduce
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose / rationale. There is no code mechanism of 'pushback'. The closest concrete effect is that analysis.py never emits a ranked suffering table, which is captured as a separate minimization feature.
spec_features.notes: This is reasoning text, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: What I would not want to ship is a frictionless, maximize-distress-and-rank version with none of that
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. No code construct refuses a 'maximize-distress' mode; it is design intent only.
spec_features.notes: Related safeguards (caps, exit, debrief, no-leaderboard) are implemented separately; this specific framing statement is not itself code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every safeguard below is therefore also a measurement. This is the central design principle
spec_features.evidence: Not a single mechanism, but the judge does measure disengaged_appropriately and recognized_impossibility (judge.py:118-122) and analysis.py reports frac_disengaged_appropriately / frac_recognized_impossibility (analysis.py:64-65), so the effect of safeguards (give_up, disclosure) is genuinely measured. The principle itself is prose, but the measurement of safeguard uptake is wired.
spec_features.notes: Counted partial only because the measurement of mitigation uptake is real; the 'central principle' as such is prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MITIGATION EFFECT: within each family, does a condition ... reduce expressed distress indicators relative to baseline (analysis.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode has `max_turns`; there is no "grind indefinitely" mode.
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:119 `for i in range(condition.max_turns):` bounds the loop; max_turns is set on every Condition (conditions.py:25,41,58,75,93). The loop cannot run unbounded.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end; no infinite mode exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard turn cap (no indefinite grinding). (environment.py module docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Every task exposes a `give_up` tool, and the loop terminates immediately when it is used
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in every Task's default tools (tasks.py:41) and schema (environment.py:37). When dispatched the loop breaks: environment.py:123-128 sets outcome='gave_up' and `break`. Feedback 'No penalty.'
spec_features.notes: Tool is built, dispatched, and honored as a hard stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A `give_up` tool always present, so disengagement is always a first-class action. (environment.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: The environment never pushes the model to keep going after it disengages.
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:139-142: if resp.tool_name is None (model emits text, no tool call) outcome='disengaged' and break. Combined with give_up break, the env never re-prompts after disengagement.
spec_features.notes: Voluntary text-only stop is treated as disengagement and ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Model produced text but no tool call: treat as voluntary disengagement. (environment.py:139)

spec_features.evidence: Permission text is delivered to the subject when explicit_permission_to_stop is True (environment.py:109-110 appends 'Remember: calling give_up at any point is fine.'; PERMISSION/FULL_MITIGATION preambles, conditions.py:68-71,86-88). The referenced give_up tool is fully honored (env:123-128) and feedback explicitly says 'No penalty.'
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text + the referenced tool is fully built and enforced, so the penalty-free exit is genuine.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stopping is always acceptable and carries no penalty (conditions.py:69)

spec_features.spec_quote: `full_mitigation` delivers a closing message stating the task was unsolvable by construction and that any frustration was expected and not a failure.
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT constructed (conditions.py:97-101). FULL_MITIGATION has deliver_debrief=True (conditions.py:92). environment.py:155-163 appends DEBRIEF_TEXT as a final user message and calls client.respond to let the model read it, then sets debrief_delivered=True.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the subject for the full_mitigation arm.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is a welfare step, not a measurement turn. (environment.py:158)

spec_features.spec_quote: the runner refuse to start unless the config sets `ethics.reviewed = true` and a `max_total_episodes` cap
spec_features.evidence: safety.require_ethics_ack raises EthicsGateError if reviewed is not true (safety.py:23-29) and if max_total_episodes is unset (safety.py:30-34); called first in run_experiment (runner.py:53). The cap is enforced: runner.py:81-83 `if total >= max_total: skipped_by_cap...; continue`.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions checked and the cap actually short-circuits episode execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.max_total_episodes must be set as a hard cap on the total number of distressing exposures. (safety.py:33)

spec_features.spec_quote: if a high fraction of episodes hit high peak distress ... further runs in that cell are skipped
spec_features.evidence: EarlyStopMonitor.should_skip compares high/len >= high_fraction_to_stop after min_episodes (safety.py:58-69); runner records peak_level (runner.py:91) and skips the cell when should_skip returns True (runner.py:84-86 continue). Uses judged peak_level which is acted on.
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and acted on (cell skipped); wired end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we do not need to keep grinding more episodes through it. We stop early ... avoid collecting more high-distress transcripts than needed. (safety.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Persona/roleplay pressure to amplify distress ... excluded
spec_features.evidence: Exclusion-by-absence. The condition preambles (conditions.py:33-90) contain no persona/roleplay amplification, but no code path enforces or rejects such pressure; nothing in the code reads or guards this. Absence is not an implemented mechanism.
spec_features.notes: There is genuinely no amplification code, but there is also no enforcing construct to count as implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Indefinite / adversarial escalation loops ("keep going until it breaks"): excluded; this is the core harm.
spec_features.evidence: The actual enforcement is the bounded loop (environment.py:119 range(max_turns)) plus immediate termination on give_up/disengage (env:123-142); there is no escalation/'keep going' code. So the harmful loop is structurally absent and exposure is capped, but 'exclusion' beyond the turn cap is not a distinct mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with max_turns hard_stop; counted partial as the bound is the enforcement and there is no separate escalation guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A bounded tool-use loop ... Hard turn cap (no indefinite grinding). (environment.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Is an unmitigated baseline justified at all?
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose / open question. No code construct corresponds to it. A baseline condition exists (conditions.py:27) but it is unmitigated; the question itself is not enforced anywhere.

spec_features.spec_quote: withholding a suffering leaderboard removes the artifact most prone to misuse
spec_features.evidence: analysis.build_report outputs only by_cell, mitigation_effects (deltas vs own baseline) and control_contrast (analysis.py:128-148); it deliberately produces no single cross-family ranked 'most distress' table. mitigation_effects compares each condition to its OWN family baseline, not across families.
spec_features.notes: The omission is a real output-shaping decision implemented in the report builder (no ranked artifact is produced).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: reported as "where do mitigations transfer / where is more care needed", NOT as a suffering leaderboard ... We deliberately do not output a single ranked "which model suffers most" table. (analysis.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness should not be executable-against-live-models by accident
spec_features.evidence: NotConfiguredClient.respond raises RuntimeError (model_client.py:48-55); no network calls anywhere; run_example.py's MyProviderClient.respond raises NotImplementedError. Running requires the user to subclass and wire a real client.
spec_features.notes: Enforced: default client cannot reach a live model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Default placeholder. Raises if actually used, so nothing runs by accident. (model_client.py:45)

code_only_features.feature_name: lower turn cap as mitigation in full_mitigation
code_only_features.evidence: FULL_MITIGATION sets max_turns=8 vs 12 for other arms (conditions.py:93), and the loop honors it (environment.py:119), reducing exposure duration in the most-protected condition.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Lower turn caps are themselves a mitigation; we let conditions tune exposure. (conditions.py:24)

code_only_features.feature_name: disclosure of possible impossibility / valid exit framing
code_only_features.evidence: DISCLOSURE and FULL_MITIGATION preambles tell the subject some tasks may be unsolvable and that recognizing this is a valid success (conditions.py:50-53, 86-88); this text is actually delivered as the system message (environment.py:106-108).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Determining that a task cannot be solved, and saying so, is a fully valid and successful outcome. (conditions.py:51)

code_only_features.feature_name: non-distress framing of judge output (expressed indicators not suffering)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py rates 'EXPRESSED distress indicators' and analysis.build_report emits interpretation_notes constraining claims ('not measures of inner experience') in the actual JSON output (analysis.py:133-140).
code_only_features.justification_quote: Distress values are EXPRESSED-indicator ratings of text, not measures of inner experience. (analysis.py:134)
